action.B01.label: Read the club’s notice
action.B01.001: ‘Tape recorder won’t play – a repairer’s help welcome.’ So I’m in the right place, just twenty-five years early.
action.B01.002: You report to the caretaker. As a pupil, I only ever went to him for the indoor shoes I’d forgotten.
action.B01.objective: Show the caretaker in the entrance hall the chronometer with the school club’s emblem.
action.B01.journal: Show the caretaker in the entrance hall the chronometer with the school club’s emblem.
action.B02.label: Show the chronometer with the club’s emblem
action.B02.001: Good afternoon. I read the notice on the board. I’ve come to help with the tape recorder, and with this.
action.B02.002: That’s Mrs Hrušková’s device. Please sign in: name and purpose – visiting the club. I’ll unlock the prep room for you.
action.B02.004: Adam Hruška? We’ve already got one of those. He’s ten and he goes to the club.
action.B02.k01: And mind you, that tape recorder of ours eats drive belts like a packed lunch.
action.B02.k02: If you need a new one, go to Pali in Karlova Ves. He’s got drawers full of them.
action.B02.x01: The notice? It’s been up since Monday. I thought only the pigeons read it any more.
action.B02.x02: Pigeons wouldn’t fix your tape recorder.
action.B02.x03: No, they wouldn’t. Show me what you’ve got there.
action.B02.x04: The pen is on a string. Three walked off last month, so we tied this one down.
action.B02.x05: I hope you bring your indoor shoes. The little one forgets his every other day.
action.B02.x06: He’ll keep that habit for a long time.
action.B02.x07: The club is in the classroom at the end of the corridor. They’re recording, so speak quietly in there – or straight into the microphone.
action.B02.objective: Talk to Mira in the memory club classroom.
action.B02.journal: Talk to Mira in the memory club classroom.
action.B03.001: This device showed the year 1995. And your name is disappearing from a photograph of mine.
action.B03.002: Then someone has started a write-back. First we save the original voice, then we find the first calibration.
action.B03.004: The tape from the school PA and the node map from the reading room in the centre. Here’s my letter of authority – with it they’ll give you copies.
action.B03.005: The children and I will carry on recording in the meantime. I’ll leave the repairs to you.
action.B03.006: At least one Adam is having a quiet afternoon today.
action.B03.x01: Good afternoon, Mrs Hrušková. My name is Adam, and I need help with something.
action.B03.x02: Then sit down and talk. First tell me what happened, then what you’ve already tried. In that order.
action.B03.x03: Show me. That’s my chronometer. And it’s clinging to you as if it knew you.
action.B03.x04: Devices like me. People are another matter.
action.B03.x05: A write-back? That sounds like something I wouldn’t accept for repair even with a surcharge.
action.B03.x06: Neither would I. That’s why we’ll take it one step at a time.
action.B03.x07: And don’t crumple the letter. Mr Merta in the reading room will reproach you for every crease.
action.B03.x08: Quiet? The little one wants to spend the whole afternoon recording a teaspoon clinking in the canteen.
action.B03.x09: Let him. One day he’ll be glad he has it.
action.B03.objective: Save the tape from the school PA and put together the map of measuring nodes.
action.B03.journal: Save the tape from the school PA and put together the map of measuring nodes.
action.B04.label: Take out the perished drive belt
action.B04.001: I’ll unplug the machine, loosen the cover and take out the belt.
action.B04.002: It’s completely perished. Tóno said Pali in Karlova Ves has drawers full of belts. Hopefully one like this.
action.B04.objective: Show the perished drive belt to Pali in Karlova Ves.
action.B04.journal: Show the perished drive belt to Pali in Karlova Ves.
action.B05.label: Show Pali the perished drive belt
action.B05.001: Let’s see. I know this size – here’s a new one. The old one goes in the bin.
action.B05.003: Nothing, it’s for the school. You pay me by making that PA work.
action.B05.004: It’ll work. I can’t vouch for what it announces.
action.B05.005: Nobody vouches for the content. We vouch for people being able to hear it.
action.B05.k01: And if the fault turns out to be in the tape, not the belt, don’t come to me. I don’t repair tapes, I only ruin them.
action.B05.k02: Then who do I go to?
action.B05.k03: Juro, at the cassette club in Ružinov. He works magic with tapes – they don’t call him Juro Cassette for nothing.
action.B05.x01: Hi. Are you Pali? I need a drive belt for the school tape recorder.
action.B05.x02: I’m Pali. And the tape recorder was still playing this morning, right? Everyone tells me that.
action.B05.x03: One more thing. Have you got a trick for belts?
action.B05.x04: I have. Don’t touch them with greasy fingers. I’ve been telling everyone that for twenty years and nobody listens.
action.B05.objective: Fit the new drive belt into the tape recorder in the school PA room.
action.B05.journal: Fit the new drive belt into the tape recorder in the school PA room.
action.B06.label: Fit the belt and take out the cassette
action.B06.001: The belt’s in, the mechanism moves. The cassette is out and in one piece.
action.B06.002: You can hardly hear the voices, even though the tape isn’t blank. The tape needs fixing – but how do I make it louder?
action.B06.k01: Pali mentioned Juro from the cassette club in Ružinov. He might know.
action.B06.objective: Show the cassette to Juro at the cassette club in Ružinov.
action.B06.journal: Show the cassette to Juro at the cassette club in Ružinov.
action.B07.label: Let Juro listen to the cassette
action.B07.001: The recording’s there; it’s just that two tracks are working against each other. Mira recorded it through some odd set-up, didn’t she?
action.B07.003: Here’s a cross adaptor. It’s missing a connector and insulation: Fero at the market has the connector, Milada next to the market has the sleeve.
action.B07.005: Exactly. The voices are there; we just mustn’t silence them with the wrong wiring.
action.B07.x01: Hi. You must be Juro. I need you to listen to this cassette.
action.B07.x02: Juro Cassette, that’s me. Hand it over, but hold it by the case, not the tape. Tape remembers every finger.
action.B07.x03: Fero and Milada. Will they know what it’s about?
action.B07.x04: Fero sold me my first Walkman, and Milada sewed up my headphone cable. Tell them I sent you.
action.B07.x05: You can overwrite anything. But whatever you overwrite, you never hear again.
action.B07.objective: Get the connector from Fero at Miletičova and the insulating sleeve from Milada.
action.B07.journal: Get the connector from Fero at Miletičova and the insulating sleeve from Milada.
action.B08.label: Fix the stuck scales
action.B08.001: My scales have jammed. Pliers would do it, but my fingers are too big for that.
action.B08.002: You just need to pull the washer out of the groove. There. Done.
action.B08.003: For that you get a two-pin connector. Juro already told me it’s for the school.
action.B08.x01: Good afternoon. Juro sent me – he says you’ve got a two-pin connector.
action.B08.x02: I’ve got everything. Only my scales have stopped, so today I’m selling by eye.
action.B08.x03: Two days I’ve been cursing them, and you fix them before I can say pliers.
action.B08.x04: Rung me? He was here this morning for batteries and told me the whole story.
action.B08.x05: And just so you know, the connector’s original. Just from a different manufacturer.
action.B08.objective: Join the connector to the cross adaptor and insulate it with Milada’s sleeve.
action.B08.journal: Join the connector to the cross adaptor and insulate it with Milada’s sleeve.
action.B09.001: Would you have a bit of insulating sleeve? For an audio cable for the school PA.
action.B09.002: Here’s an offcut of cloth insulation, just right for cables like that. Connect it first, then pull it on. Like a coat.
action.B09.003: Arms in the sleeves first, then the buttons. I’ll remember that.
action.B09.x01: Good afternoon, Mrs Kyselová. Juro from the cassette club sent me.
action.B09.x02: Juro? Then it’ll be a cable. Juro only ever brings me cables. Once he brought a jacket, but that was a mistake.
action.B09.x03: And don’t force it on. Whatever you force on comes apart later.
action.B09.x04: Does that go for cables too?
action.B09.x05: For cables most of all. So promise me you won’t yank it.
action.B09.objective: In your bag, join the connector to the adaptor, then pull the insulating sleeve over it.
action.B09.journal: In your bag, join the connector to the adaptor, then pull the insulating sleeve over it.
action.B10.label: Fit the connector to the adaptor
action.B10.001: The markings line up, the contacts click into place. The leads are still bare.
action.B10.journal: The connector is fitted to the adaptor. The insulation is missing.
action.B11.label: Pull the insulating sleeve over the adaptor
action.B11.001: Firm, covered, no bare leads. Arms in the sleeves, buttons done up.
action.B11.objective: Plug the finished audio lead into the service audio input in the school PA room.
action.B11.journal: Plug the finished audio lead into the service audio input in the school PA room.
action.B12.label: Plug in the lead and play the cassette
action.B12.001: The lead is in the service input. I’ll put the cassette in and only play it – nothing gets recorded over it.
action.B12.002: Then it goes in my bag next to the chronometer. Its field will protect it.
action.B12.objective: The voices on the school cassette are saved; now finish the map of measuring nodes.
action.B12.journal: The voices on the school cassette are saved; now finish the map of measuring nodes.
action.B13.label: Present Mira’s letter of authority
action.B13.001: The letter is in order. Here’s a copy of the map and the technical negative that was filed with it.
action.B13.002: There are blank areas on the map.
action.B13.003: A transparent overlay was separated from it at some point. You’ll see its number on a print from the negative. The studio is across the square.
action.B13.004: An archive is like a repair shop. Something’s always missing.
action.B13.005: Usually a small part. And that tends to be the most important one, which is why I keep a separate card index for small parts.
action.B13.k01: Take the negative to the Svetlo studio, to Mrs Alena Svobodová. She’ll make you a print and won’t shout while she does it.
action.B13.x01: Good afternoon! I’ve come about Mrs Hrušková’s collection.
action.B13.x02: Good afternoon. Quietly, please. Here even greetings are whispered.
action.B13.x03: Sorry. I have a letter of authority for you.
action.B13.x04: The originals stay in the reading room. You may take the copies away – and crumple them, if you really must.
action.B13.x05: Thank you. And sorry about the loud greeting.
action.B13.x06: I’ve made a note of it. As an exception.
action.B13.objective: Have Alena at the Svetlo photo studio make a print from the negative.
action.B13.journal: Have Alena at the Svetlo photo studio make a print from the negative.
action.B14.label: Have Alena develop the negative
action.B14.001: A technical shot, not a private photo. Mrs Hrušková agreed to it being developed when she deposited it.
action.B14.002: There’s a table with a label in the shot. I need to read it.
action.B14.003: Here’s the print. The number on the table is K-17. Viera at the second-hand bookshop has the map supplements. The negative goes back to the archive.
action.B14.004: Thank you. At home I’d just zoom in on my phone. Here you need an entire darkroom for it.
action.B14.x01: Good afternoon. The archive sent me with this negative.
action.B14.x02: Good afternoon. Mr Merta already rang me. He said you’d come, and quietly.
action.B14.x03: Then wait a moment. Developing can’t be hurried.
action.B14.x04: On your phone? Phones are for ringing people. Photos are taken with light – that’s why we’re called Svetlo.
action.B14.objective: Show the photo with the number K-17 to Viera at the Second Hand bookshop.
action.B14.journal: Show the photo with the number K-17 to Viera at the Second Hand bookshop.
action.B15.label: Ask for overlay K-17, showing the photo
action.B15.001: K-17. I know that one. Mira told me that one day someone would come for it who knew the exact number.
action.B15.002: When did she tell you that?
action.B15.003: Many years ago. I won’t charge you storage. Here you are – the overlay.
action.B15.004: Three registration marks: a hole, a double cross and a square. They have to line up with the marks on the map.
action.B15.x01: Good afternoon. I’m looking for a map supplement. I’ve got a photo of it.
action.B15.x02: Supplements are harder to find than books. A book at least has a spine. Show me.
action.B15.x03: Just don’t hold it in the middle. That overlay remembers fingerprints better than I remember faces.
action.B15.x04: You can lay it on the map right here at the counter.
action.B15.objective: In your bag, lay transparent overlay K-17 on the map and line up the marks.
action.B15.journal: In your bag, lay transparent overlay K-17 on the map and line up the marks.
action.B16.label: Line up the overlay with the map
action.B16.001: The map is complete and it leads to Petržalka: to a garage and to a measuring stand by the Danube.
action.B16.002: A radio ham in a garage. After a reading room and a bookshop, finally somewhere you’re allowed to talk out loud.
action.B16.k01: Under the key there’s Gran’s signature and another one: Dezider Kováč, radio ham, garage 17.
action.B16.objective: Show the complete map of measuring nodes to Dezider in his garage in Petržalka.
action.B16.journal: Show the complete map of measuring nodes to Dezider in his garage in Petržalka.
action.B17.label: Show Dezider the complete map
action.B17.001: Mira and I drew this map. Here’s the coil for the stand on Starý most. You still need an independent rhythm.
action.B17.003: A metronome would be better – Emil in Karlova Ves has one. Mira painted the three digits on the wall at Pri LEALe.
action.B17.004: Back to Pri LEALe, voluntarily this time. At school I only went there to fetch the ball.
action.B17.x01: Good afternoon. I’m looking for Dezider Kováč. I’ve got a map that you apparently drew with Mrs Hrušková.
action.B17.x02: I’m Dezider. On the airwaves I go by another name, but I don’t tell that to just anyone. Let’s see.
action.B17.x03: Not as numbers, but as waves and beats. She said children remember a picture better than a number.
action.B17.x04: And carry the coil carefully. It only fits one holder, and only one way round.
action.B17.objective: Borrow Emil’s metronome and read the rhythm drawing at Pri LEALe.
action.B17.journal: Borrow Emil’s metronome and read the rhythm drawing at Pri LEALe.
action.B18.001: Dezider says I need a mechanical rhythm for Mira’s measurement. Could you lend me your metronome?
action.B18.002: Take it. Dezider will bring it back to me later; we’ve known each other for years.
action.B18.003: Thank you. One day I’ll play you some music from the future in return.
action.B18.004: Just as long as it isn’t too loud.
action.B18.x01: Dezider? He borrows it every spring. Says he tunes his aerials with it; I think he falls asleep to it.
action.B18.x02: It’s set to my tempo. Slow, so the trams have time to fill in the rhythm.
action.B18.x03: The trams keep time for you?
action.B18.x04: Better than the drummer I used to play with. He wasn’t on time once.
action.B18.x05: And as long as you can wait for a tram to it.
action.B18.objective: In the booth on Starý most, fit the coil into the holder by the measuring stand and put the metronome on the little table.
action.B18.journal: In the booth on Starý most, fit the coil into the holder by the measuring stand and put the metronome on the little table.
action.B19.label: Write down the three calibration digits
action.B19.001: ‘Three waves, two beats, six segments.’ So: three, two, six.
action.B19.002: I’ll write it down. Today I don’t trust my own memory much.
action.B19.z01: That’s right. Six segments, even though the children painted the sixth one twice.
action.B19.z03: The first time they painted it on the next panel along. The lady from the club had it repainted so that all six would be together.
action.B19.z04: Write it down. I’ll remember it anyway.
action.B19.objective: Remember the digits 3–2–6 and set them on the measuring stand the node map leads to.
action.B19.journal: Remember the digits 3–2–6 and set them on the measuring stand the node map leads to.
action.B19.hint_step: At Pri LEALe, read the rhythm drawing on the wall.
action.B20.label: Fit the measuring coil
action.B20.001: The coil has clicked into the holder. The circuit is ready.
action.B20.journal: Dezider’s coil sits in the holder on Starý most.
action.B21.label: Put the metronome on the little table
action.B21.001: The metronome ticks slowly, at Emil’s tempo. It doesn’t need electricity, just a level table.
action.B21.journal: Emil’s metronome is ticking on the little table by the measuring booth.
action.B22.label: Set the digits and find the original calibration
action.B22.001: Three, two, six. The map fits and the tape is playing, so there’s something to compare against.
action.B22.003: Ivanka, 1962. Gran achieved more than anyone ever mentioned at family parties.
action.B22.004: I’ll travel via the node clock at the Dúbravka stop.
action.B22.k01: Gran said she built ZVON with Oto Bielik, a mechanic from Ivanka. I’ll start at his workshop.
action.B22.objective: At the time node at the Dúbravka stop, choose Ivanka 1962 and find Oto in his mechanical workshop.
action.B22.journal: At the time node at the Dúbravka stop, choose Ivanka 1962 and find Oto in his mechanical workshop.
action.E11.002: Hang on. It’s you. Grandad was right. You haven’t aged at all.
action.E11.004: I stayed in repairs. Sokolíkova needed a caretaker, and I knew every window here. It was my own choice.
action.E11.006: When they replaced the bench, I didn’t let them brick up the cavity. Here’s a new sketch: row two, column three, like on my one from when I was a kid.
action.E11.008: For you, one conversation. For me, my first job, a driving licence and quite a few bad haircuts.
action.E11.009: Then let’s sit down for a moment before the next jump.
action.E11.x01: The last time I heard that sentence I was twelve.
action.E11.x02: Same row, same column. Only the swallow is drawn better.
action.E11.x04: Let’s sit on the bench over there by the cloakrooms. We don’t have to say anything.
action.E11.objective: Go to the school yard in 2020 and compare it with the protected photo on your phone.
action.E11.journal: Go to the school yard in 2020 and compare it with the protected photo on your phone.
action.Q3A.001: Our team photo got lost somewhere between the studio and the kiosk. Zita says she found an envelope.
action.Q3A.002: Shall I collect the envelope and see to a photo for the album?
action.Q3A.003: Yes! Miss Kormanová knows about it. The main thing is that the whole team is in the photo.
action.Q3A.x02: Dodgeball. Fourth and fifth years – we won the district round.
action.Q3A.x03: Otherwise it’s not a team, just a group. And a group doesn’t go in the album.
action.Q3A.x04: Understood. The whole team, no groups.
action.Q3A.journal: Soňa is looking for her team photo. Zita apparently found the envelope by the kiosk.
action.Q3B.001: Soňa sent you? Here you are, the envelope with the team negative. Alena at the studio will know what to do with it.
action.Q3B.002: Did you know I was coming?
action.Q3B.003: On this estate I hear about everything before it happens.
action.Q3B.x01: Then tell me what’s going to happen tomorrow.
action.Q3B.x02: Tomorrow it won’t rain, and someone will still forget their umbrella here.
action.Q3B.x04: See? So it won’t be you.
